description: A valid four-entry identity chain (SPEC §6.2 to §6.4) with composite keys. A device-signed entry's k is the device's 32-byte Ed25519 component: look its composite key up in the chain state before the entry (for genesis, in genesis's own add-device). A recovery-signed entry's k is the 1,984-byte composite public key: SHA-256(k) must equal the current commitment. Every `s` is a composite signature over JCS(["tieroute/v2", t, b]). In add-device, `key` must equal the last 32 bytes of `pub`.

entries.note: genesis, signed by device 1, commits to recovery key 1
recovery key 1 removes device 2 and commits to recovery key 2; k is recovery key 1's composite public key, and SHA-256(k) equals the genesis commitment
self-rotation: device 1 replaces its own key with device 3 (calm notice, SPEC §6.4.1)

identity_id_derivation: "tr:" || lowercase base32 (RFC 4648, no padding) of the first 15 bytes of SHA-256 of the genesis `signed` text (JCS)
notice: Test vectors for Tieroute wire version 2 (SPEC version 2.0, draft). These keys are public: never use them for anything real.
